lines.text: Zophar the Naamathite calls Job's speech a stream of words and says Job claims to be pure in God's sight.
Zophar wishes God would speak against Job, and says God exacts from Job less than his iniquity deserves.
Zophar says God's deep things are higher than the heavens, deeper than Sheol, and wider than the sea.
Zophar says if God imprisons Job, many can stop Him, and he compares a witless man to a wild donkey's colt.
Zophar tells Job to put away the staff in his hand, and says the wicked will hope for a second chance.
